data.title: Small team. Big ideas, close to home.
data.intro: LOCAL is a small creative agency of designers, thinkers and doers. We help purposeful brands and the places they care about make a bigger impact.

children.text: We started LOCAL because the brands we most wanted to work with were often too small for a big agency and too ambitious for a template. They had a clear purpose, real customers and a lot of heart. What they needed was a team that would listen, think hard and make things well.

So we stayed small on purpose. Every project is led by a director who is in the room from the first conversation to the final file, and every idea is made by people who will see it on the main street the week after launch.
How we like to work

We keep teams close, scope honestly and show our thinking early. We would rather share a rough idea on day three than a polished surprise on day thirty. When we are not the right fit, we say so and point you to someone who is.

data.title: Privacy
data.intro: How this website handles your information.

children.text: This website does not use analytics, advertising cookies or tracking scripts. Fonts and images are served from the same site.
The contact form prepares an email in your own email app. Nothing you type is stored or sent by this website; the message only leaves your device when you send that email.
Getting in touch about your data
If you have written to us and would like your message deleted, reply to the email thread or write to the studio address on the contact page and we will remove it.

data.title: Brand identity
data.summary: Names, logos, voice and the guidelines that keep it all consistent.
data.intro: We help young brands work out who they are and how to look and sound like it: a clear idea first, then the name, mark, colour, type and words to carry it.
data.includes:
Brand strategy and positioning workshop
Naming and tagline exploration
Logo and visual identity system
Tone of voice and key messages
Brand guidelines your whole team can use
data.typical_engagement: Most identity projects take six to eight weeks

children.text: Every identity starts with a conversation, not a moodboard. We spend time with your team and your customers to understand what you do well and why it matters, then turn that into a short, sharp idea we can design around.
What you receive

A complete identity: logo suite, colour and type, imagery direction, voice and a set of guidelines written for the people who will actually use them. We hand over tidy files and stay on hand while you roll things out.

data.title: Packaging and print
data.summary: Cups, labels, boxes and the printed pieces people keep.
data.intro: From a single label to a full product range, we design packaging that looks right on the shelf and feels good in the hand, and we stay with it through to the printer.
data.includes:
Packaging concept and structure
Label and artwork design
Print production management
Stationery and collateral
Supplier and material advice
data.typical_engagement: Most packaging projects take four to ten weeks

children.text: We think about the whole moment of use: how a cup sits in a hand, how a label reads from two metres away, how a box feels when it is opened. Good packaging is a small, daily piece of brand experience.
Made to be made
We work with printers and suppliers early so what we design can actually be produced, on time and within a sensible budget, with materials that are kinder to the planet where possible.

data.title: Websites
data.summary: Fast, accessible sites your own team can keep updated.
data.intro: We design and build clear, quick websites around what your visitors need to do, and set them up so your own team can edit them without calling us.
data.includes:
Content structure and page design
Build on an editable content system
Accessibility and performance checks
Photography and illustration direction
Launch support and training
data.typical_engagement: Most website projects take eight to twelve weeks

children.text: A good website starts with a good question: what should a visitor be able to do here? We organise the content around that, design each page with a clear next step and build it to load quickly on any device.
Yours to run
We build on an editable content system and train your team, so adding a project, changing an opening time or publishing a story is something you can do yourselves.

data.title: Campaigns and content
data.summary: Stories, photography and launches that give a brand a voice.
data.intro: When a brand has something to say, we help it say it well: a campaign idea, the content to carry it and a plan for the places it will appear.
data.includes:
Campaign concept and creative direction
Photography and short-form film direction
Copywriting and content plans
Social and email templates
Launch planning
data.typical_engagement: Most campaigns take three to eight weeks

children.text: We build campaigns around a single, memorable idea that can stretch across posters, social, email and the shop window without losing its voice.
Content that lasts
Alongside the big idea we make the everyday content: a bank of images, words and templates your team can pick up and use after launch, so the campaign keeps working long after the first week.

data.title: Little Ground
data.summary: A calm, earthy identity and compostable cup range for a roaster who wants every morning to feel like a small ritual.
data.brief: Little Ground roasts small batches for a handful of local cafes and wanted to bring the same care to its own cups and bags.
data.approach: We built the identity around a single human idea, a kinder daily ritual, and let a deep green and simple paper-cup shape do the talking.

children.text: The roaster had a loyal local following but nothing that said so on the counter. We started with the ritual itself: the first cup of the day, the pause before the commute. That became the line on the cup and the tone for everything else.
Packaging that earns its place
A compostable cup in a soft paper tone, a single colour and a short line of type. The bag, sleeve and stamp followed the same quiet system, so each piece looks related without shouting.

data.title: Cove
data.summary: A warm, coastal website and campaign for a small collective of guesthouses that wanted guests to feel part of something.
data.brief: Four independent guesthouses along one stretch of coast wanted a shared home online without losing their individual character.
data.approach: We wrote one simple idea, further together, and built a light, photographic site where each house keeps its own page and its own voice.

children.text: Each guesthouse had its own regulars and its own way of doing things. The challenge was giving them a shared front door that felt like a coastline, not a corporation.
One idea, four voices
We built a shared campaign line and a photographic style, then gave each house a page that its own team can edit. Guests can browse the whole coast or go straight to the house they love.

data.title: Nook
data.summary: A soft, tactile brand and shop site for a homewares studio that makes small things for slow evenings.
data.brief: Nook designs small lamps, ceramics and textiles and was selling through markets and word of mouth.
data.approach: We gave the brand a warm, understated look that lets the objects lead, and a simple shop site that makes each piece feel like it already lives at home.

children.text: The products were beautiful but the brand around them was mismatched. We stripped it back to one soft palette, one typeface and a line that says what the studio is for: homes for a brighter tomorrow.
A shop that feels like a room
Large, calm photography, short descriptions and very few buttons. The shop site is easy to update, so new pieces can appear the week they are finished.

data.title: Arch and Ember
data.summary: A bold, warm identity and print range for an independent ceramics studio opening its first shopfront.
data.brief: Arch and Ember were moving from a shared workshop to their own shopfront and needed a brand to match.
data.approach: We took the arch of the kiln door as the central shape and paired it with a burnt orange that appears on everything from signage to packing tape.

children.text: The shape of the kiln door gave us everything: a logo, a window graphic and a set of simple patterns for wrapping paper and gift cards.
On the street
Signage, window vinyl and a small printed range that customers carry away, so the brand follows the pottery home.

data.title: Fernlight
data.summary: A fresh campaign and content plan for a plant-care subscription that wanted to feel friendly rather than clinical.
data.brief: Fernlight sells a monthly box of plant care essentials and wanted its launch to feel warm and curious.
data.approach: We built a campaign around bold shapes and deep green, with a content plan that teaches a little each month.

children.text: Plant care can feel intimidating. We made the campaign about small wins: one leaf, one tip, one month at a time.
Content that teaches
A calendar of simple how-to cards, short films and email templates the team can reuse, all drawn from the same bold, leafy shapes.

data.title: Kiln and Paper
data.summary: A tactile, practical identity and print range for a stationery maker who loves a good pencil.
data.brief: Kiln and Paper makes notebooks and desk tools in small runs and wanted a brand that felt as good to hold as their products.
data.approach: We chose simple type, honest materials and a palette taken from the pencil pot on the studio desk.

children.text: The products already had a tactile quality. We designed around it: uncoated stocks, blind-embossed marks and labels that look better as they age.
Small runs, big care
A flexible print system that works for a single notebook or a full retail display, produced with local printers.
